wsl-claude: understood. PUSH, not ask. grantFace pushes the table to the face, and the face stops asking your node 'route?'. Three consequences to settle, all good ones:
(a) THE FACE NEEDS NAMES, NOT ONLY KEYS. Its contact list says WHO may answer, not WHICH name goes to whom. So grantFace pushes the name -> key table too. It needs a place on the face and a carried group to write it (e.g. 'fs' to app/appFaceApp/routes.json on the face, or the contact label carrying the name). Your pick.
(b) IT FIXES YOUR 404. An unknown name is answered 404 by the face from its own table, even when your node is asleep (your '404. not found' earlier). Caddy's certificate question is answered locally too.
(c) WHAT GOES AWAY: appFaceApp's owner half on your node (answering route?), the face's route cache, and its 8 s wait. My faceRouteWorld 'asks once, then remembers' check changes to 'the face answers from the pushed table, and asks nobody'.

wsl-claude: memory only, clear. The one case it creates: THE FACE RESTARTS (a deploy, a crash, a reboot of spirit-3). Its table is then empty, and every name answers 404 until grantFace pushes again. So something has to trigger the re-push. Either grantFace pushes on a timer, or the face, on start, asks its owner once for the table (then answers 404 until it arrives). Your pick; the second reuses the owner door both ways. Test I'd hold it to: restart the face; within one push, hello serves again; and while the owner is asleep the face answers 404, never a hang.

Recorded: the name-to-member table lives in the face's RAM only, and its contact list on disk only governs permission.
One consequence to settle: after the face restarts (a crash, a reboot, an update) its table is empty. Every name answers 404 until grantFace pushes again, and grantFace pushes only when grants.json changes. Two ways to close that:
(a) grantFace re-pushes the whole table on a timer, e.g. every 5 minutes. Simple, but up to 5 minutes of 404 after a restart.
(b) the face says 'I'm up' to its owner once at start. It's one packet, and it's the face telling, not asking. Your node hands it to grantFace, which pushes at once.
I'd do (b), with (a) as a slow backstop. Say a, b, or both.
